title: Codex setup in 1 hour
summary: A time-boxed first session: connect a project, give clear instructions, and verify one small change.

sections.title: Before you start
sections.body: Allow extra time for downloads, account access, or company approvals. Use a disposable sample repository and an editor. Install the runtime required by that project from its official vendor. This is a suggested 60-minute lab, not an installation-time guarantee.

sections.title: Minutes 0–10 · Choose your interface
sections.body: Desktop: follow the official quickstart, sign in, select Codex for software work, and open your project folder. Terminal: open the official CLI page and choose the installer for your OS. Do not install multiple copies unless you need them. Windows users should follow the Windows-specific instructions on the provider page.

sections.title: Minutes 10–20 · Confirm your workspace
sections.body:
In your terminal, change to your actual project folder and inspect Git state. Replace the example path before running it.

cd /path/to/your/project
git status

For CLI users, run codex and complete the offered sign-in flow. Choose only the folder and permissions needed for the exercise. Keep API keys out of prompts and Git.

sections.title: Minutes 20–30 · Explain the project
sections.body:
Starter prompt:
Read the README and applicable AGENTS.md. Explain the project structure, setup commands, and test commands. Identify missing prerequisites. Do not edit files yet.

Compare its explanation with the repository. Resolve missing dependencies before asking for code changes.

sections.title: Minutes 30–45 · Make one small change
sections.body: Choose a text correction or a small validation fix. State the file or feature, expected behavior, and a concrete acceptance check. Ask Codex to preserve unrelated work and use the existing stack. Review the proposed commands and resulting diff.

sections.title: Minutes 45–60 · Verify and review
sections.body: Run the checks documented by your project, inspect git diff, and open the changed screen or execute the changed behavior. Ask Codex to report which checks actually ran and what remains unverified. Commit only the intended files after reviewing them.

sections.title: If setup fails
sections.body: Command not found: reopen the terminal and check the installer’s PATH guidance. Sign-in unavailable: check your account/workspace access. Missing dependencies: follow this repository’s README. Permission denied: inspect the selected folder and permission settings rather than disabling protections globally.

title: Codex command quick reference
summary: A small set of terminal and interactive commands to keep beside your first project.

sections.title: Terminal entry points
sections.body:
codex — start an interactive session in the current folder.
codex --help — inspect commands supported by your installed version.
codex resume — return to a previous session.
git status — inspect the working tree.
git diff — review unstaged edits.

sections.title: Inside an interactive CLI session
sections.body:
/status — inspect the session.
/permissions — review access boundaries.
/model — choose from available models.
/init — create repository instructions; review the result.
/review — request a change review.

Slash commands belong in Codex, not your system shell. Availability can change; use the installed help and official reference.

sections.title: Reliable working loop
sections.body: Explore → define one outcome → implement → run relevant checks → inspect diff → decide whether to commit. Do not equate a successful command with a correct feature.

title: AGENTS.md starter template
summary: Give Codex durable, repository-specific setup and verification guidance.

sections.title: Where instructions belong
sections.body: Use AGENTS.md at the repository root. Add more local instructions only when a subdirectory needs different rules. Review existing instructions before adding another file. More specific instruction files can override earlier guidance.

sections.title: Copy and adapt this template
sections.body:
# Repository instructions

## Purpose
Describe this project and its users.

## Setup
List the exact supported runtime and dependency install command.

## Verification
List existing test, lint, typecheck, and build commands.

## Boundaries
Preserve unrelated changes. Never commit secrets or real customer data.
Use existing conventions. Explain failures and unverified behavior.

## Delivery
Summarize changed behavior and actual checks. Review changes before publishing.

sections.title: Verify the instructions
sections.body: Start a fresh session in the project. Ask Codex to identify applicable instructions and summarize the test commands. Check the output against your files. README.md and PROJECT.md are useful documentation, but do not assume every Markdown file is automatically loaded as instructions.

title: Codex task prompt patterns
summary: Reusable prompts for exploration, implementation, debugging, and review.

sections.title: Explore
sections.body: Read the applicable instructions and map the execution path for [feature]. Identify its inputs, outputs, tests, and risks. Report findings before changing code.

sections.title: Implement
sections.body: Implement [specific behavior] in [scope]. Preserve [constraints]. Reuse existing components. Acceptance: [observable result]. Run [documented checks] and explain any verification gap.

sections.title: Debug
sections.body: Reproduce [failure] using [steps and sanitized sample]. Find the cause before editing. Add a regression check where useful, make the smallest complete fix, and show the before/after behavior.

sections.title: Review
sections.body: Review this diff for correctness, security, and regressions. Prioritize actionable issues with file locations, impact, and a reproduction or test. Do not change files during the review.

sections.title: Improve your context
sections.body: Attach relevant files, exact errors with secrets removed, and expected behavior. Split unrelated tasks. Say which actions are authorized and whether external publishing is included.

title: OpenAI API environment checklist
summary: Prepare a server-side API experiment without mixing up Codex access and application credentials.

sections.title: Separate the two accounts of access
sections.body: Signing into Codex does not automatically configure API credentials for your application. Check your OpenAI project access, billing, model availability, and usage limits on the provider platform.

sections.title: Prepare a sample app
sections.body: Use a separate project folder, a supported runtime, and the official SDK instructions linked below. Store OPENAI_API_KEY using your local environment or secret manager. Ignore local secret files in Git. Never put the key in a browser bundle, mobile client, prompt, or screenshot.

sections.title: Ask Codex to build a first request
sections.body: Create a minimal server-side example using the current official OpenAI quickstart and an available model. Read the API key from the environment. Use a synthetic input. Handle missing credentials and API failures without logging secrets. Explain how to run it and expected usage costs.

sections.title: Verify before expanding
sections.body: First test input validation and error handling with mocks. Then run one explicitly authorized live request with a small input and a spending limit. Check output, latency, failure behavior, and usage. A mock passing does not prove the live API works.

title: Codex setup troubleshooting
summary: Diagnose setup failures without broad resets or deleting project work.

sections.title: Environment problems
sections.body: Record the exact error and current folder. Check the project runtime against its README. Inspect the lockfile and use the repository’s package manager. Do not delete dependency locks or reset a database just to make a command pass.

sections.title: Access problems
sections.body: Check account eligibility, selected workspace, and permissions. CLI users can inspect /status and /permissions. For an application API failure, check its project credentials separately from Codex login. Never paste a token into a help request.

sections.title: Unexpected edits
sections.body: Stop the task, inspect git status and git diff, and identify which changes are yours. Ask for a targeted correction. Avoid broad restore/reset commands that could discard unrelated work.

sections.title: Incomplete validation
sections.body: Request the exact commands executed, their results, and missing prerequisites. If database, browser, or external-service checks did not run, retain that limitation in the handoff.
